findings.oracle: Real input b'\x48\x31\xc0\x48\x89\xe5\xc3' fed through live capstone using the (arch,mode) returned by auto_detect_arch for 'x86_64'; independent oracle is the x86-64 ISA itself (verified mode-sensitive: 64-bit decodes xor rax,rax/mov rbp,rsp/ret vs 32-bit dec eax/xor eax,eax/...); assertion is exact-equality on [(0x1000,'xor','rax, rax'),(0x1003,'mov','rbp, rsp'),(0x1006,'ret','')], so a corrupted _CAPSTONE_ARCH_MODE_MAP['x86_64'] entry changes the mnemonics and fails.

Renamed to test_validate_r2_argument_rejects_control_chars so pytest discovers and runs it; drives 11 rizin command-control metacharacters (; \n \r @ | ~ ` > < $ #) each embedded in a safe identifier through the real validate_r2_argument, asserting ToolError is raised and the field name 'symbol' surfaces in the message, plus a leading '!' shell-escape case.

Renamed to test_validate_r2_argument_accepts_safe_strings so pytest discovers and runs it; drives real safe identifiers ('symbol_name42','main','0x401000','sub.text-1','_GLOBAL__sub_I_main',''  and 'name!bang') through validate_r2_argument and asserts byte-for-byte identity (return == input) to guard against silent stripping/rewriting on the accept path.

hasattr smoke test replaced by two real gates that call doc.search_text_encoded on a real UTF-16LE buffer 'Hello World Hello' (16-byte pad): asserts exact offsets/lengths [(16,10),(40,10)] and case-sensitivity ([] for 'hello' sensitive vs [(16,10),(40,10)] insensitive). TestBuildNumericFormat now feeds each produced format string into struct.pack/unpack/calcsize and asserts canonical bytes against the binary-representation oracle (e.g. 0x12345678 LE -> 78 56 34 12, INT64_MIN, two's-complement -2 BE -> ff fe, struct.error on overflow/negative, ValueError on size 3).
